unit.why: Within a compilation of teachings on anger, the division quotes a short anecdote from the Lurianic circle: a disciple performs yihudim on Tisha B'Av night, Samael provokes him to anger, and the Ari (מרן) tells him he caused a murder. It ends with a homiletic citation from Noam Megadim.
unit.boundary_note: part of an ongoing anthology of sayings on anger; previous and next divisions are teachings

stories.start_quote: וכן אירע פ״א לתלמיד שהי׳ יושב
stories.end_quote: ועשה תשובה גם על זה עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: A disciple of the Ari performed yihudim and wrote Torah secrets on the night of Tisha B'Av, easing his mourning because the fast was postponed and a circumcision fell that day. He thereby entered Samael's domain, and Samael provoked him to great anger that week, which caused one wicked man to stab another to death. The Ari revealed this to him and he repented.
